test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**​Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

Your homework must be completed before the deadline.

options.text: You must complete your homework before the deadline.
Your homework should be completed before the deadline.
Your homework must have been completed before the deadline.
You must have completed your homework before the deadline.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The type of the sentence is **modal passive voice,** and the tense of the given sentence is present simple.
 
• The **subject** of the given sentence is **"your homework**" and the **object **will be **“you” **as it suggests somebody else saying your homework.
 
• The format of passive voice for a modal verb is: **Subject + modal verb + be + V3 (past participle form of verb) + by + Object .**
 
• The format of active voice for a modal verb: **Subject (Objective case) + modal verb + V1 (base form of the verb) + object (Subjective case).**
 
• Example: 
 
 
• "The door must be locked by you." (Passive Voice).
 
• "You must lock the door." (Active Voice) 
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is- *“You must complete your homework before the deadline.”***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 ("Your homework should be completed before the deadline.")** changes the modal verb from 'must' to 'should', altering the degree of necessity.
 
• **Option 3 ("Your homework must have been completed before the deadline.") **implies that the action has already been completed, which is not the original intent of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4 ("You must have completed your homework before the deadline.") **also implies completion, suggesting a conclusion drawn about a past event rather than instructing future action.
